about: The graduale of the formulary “Sunday within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: You are fairer in beauty than the sons of men; grace has been poured out upon Your lips. My heart has uttered a good word; I recite my works to the King: my tongue is the pen of a scribe who writes swiftly.

ex.w001: The comparison comes from prae, even though speciosus itself is not a comparative form. The following lábiis tuis (“Thy lips”) makes the address clear. “Thou art” is understood, not written in the Latin.
ex.w012: The heart is pictured as pouring out words. The following image of the tongue as a scribe’s pen continues this picture of speech arising from within.
ex.w019: In this image of spoken words and a scribe’s pen, “works” refers to the speaker’s compositions. The Latin is plural.
